newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's public debt ends 1996 at 33.3 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's public debt ends 1996 at 33.3 pct of GDP.

text.p: Mexico's total public debt fell about 11 percentage points to 33.3 pct of gross domestic product (GDP) at the end of 1996, the Finance Ministry said in a statement released on Thursday.
The Ministry said that at the end of 1995 the nation's total public debt as a percentage of GDP was 44.0 percent.

It said the 1996 primary surplus -- the difference between total revenue and expenses, excluding debt servicing charges -- was 108.48 billion pesos, compared with 85.80 billion pesos at the end of the previous year.
The ministry said the public sector deficit was equivalent to 0.09 percent of GDP.
It said financing costs of the public debt were 110.46 billion pesos in 1996.
"Its part (financing costs) of the total net expenditures fell to 18.9 percentage points in 1996 from 20.1 percentage points in 1995," the ministry said in its statement.

The ministry said that federal government operations showed a deficit of 12.46 billion pesos in the year, due to a primary surplus of 81.83 billion pesos and public debt financing costs of 94.29 billion pesos.

Federal government revenues were 392.94 billion pesos in 1996, and the finance ministry added that revenues showed a sharp increase in the second half of the year as the economy improved and tax collections rose.
At the end of 1996, gross external public debt was $98.28 billion, $2.65 billion less than at the end of 1995.
The ministry said its short-term debt declined 30.6 percent to $4.99 billion at the end of 1996, compared to $7.20 billion at the end of 1995.
It said gross external public debt fell to 26.7 percent of GDP at the end of 1996 compared to 36.6 percent at the end of 1995.
Net external public debt was $89.75 billion at the end of 1996, it said.
At the end of 1996, gross internal debt was 192.16 billion pesos. The federal government's part of this was 179.4 billion pesos, the ministry said.
It said the average maturity of the internal debt rose to 305 days at the end of the year compared to 282 days in the last week of 1995.
